analysis:
The supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md, lines 460-998. The only visible PR change is a documentation edit around head lines 11-25. It renames the v0.10.2 candidate to v0.10.3 and adds a release note about an M5 Metal kernel compile crash. It also records submodule pin moves for libs/mlx-swift and libs/mlx. Those pins were not supplied and are not part of this review, so the visible change does not show whether they introduce or fix any security behavior.

Because the diff is a changelog only, no code, crypto, authorization, attestation or cache path changes in the visible evidence. I mapped the changelog text against the retained threat model entries, mainly T-041 (prefix cache), TB-007 (inference engine) and T-043 (watchdog). The changelog describes the encrypted SSD prefix store as default on for GLM, with DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 as the opt-out. That matches the T-041 posture and does not widen it. The base text also mentions DEBUG-only DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE and says release builds do not contain that path. That is a claim about the source, which was not supplied, so I cannot verify it here. The changelog also mentions the watchdog auto-updating and restarting a crash-looping provider (T-043 context), and the KV-backend guard that clears on a version change. These are descriptive and add no new surface in the visible diff.

Remaining unverified contracts are the MLX submodule bumps (mlx-swift 4926d3d9, mlx 31f550af) and the actual code behind the described kernel fix. A reviewer should check those pins against the supply-chain and build-provenance assumptions (T-034, A-011). I raise no finding because no concrete regression is evidenced.
